A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching core methods, equations and experiments. All supplied pages are readable. v2 ends after its references; v3 additionally includes supplementary Sections 6–13, whose contents can be compared reliably against the supplied v2.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction and novel-view synthesis results on Waymo-NOTR and KITTI, together with component ablations in Tables 1–3 and qualitative results in Figure 3.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and additionally reports static-scene evaluation, runtime comparisons, tracking analyses, editing demonstrations and failure cases in its supplement.

M1.justification: The GLEE/LiDAR/ICP tracking pipeline, isotropic Gaussians, HexPlane motion model and staged optimization remain unchanged. The supplement documents editing capabilities, human-motion handling and loss implementation without establishing a revision to the proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 adds novel-view evaluation on Waymo-NOTR static32 and qualitative car removal, movement and substitution demonstrations (Section 6 and Figure 4). These extend coverage within the existing driving domain; dynamic32 and KITTI coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their comparator sets. New supplementary comparisons evaluate Street Gaussians with CasTrack and a rigid-transformation variant using the proposed method's 2D-derived trajectories (Tables 6–7). These are additional configurations of an existing comparison method.

E3.justification: The original splits, training budgets and rendering metrics are retained. Supplementary experiments introduce translation/rotation error evaluation capped at 1 m/30 degrees, maximum penalties for missing detections, and runtime comparisons on the same device. The new CasTrack experiment uses KITTI pretraining, unlike the retained nuScenes-pretrained VoxelNext configuration.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained Table 3 ablations, v3 adds tracker-choice testing, tracking-error distributions, and comparison of rigid motion with HexPlane using 2D-derived trajectories (Tables 6–7 and Figure 5). Editing demonstrations and a human-motion failure case further expand the diagnostic evidence (Figures 4 and 6).

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Figure 5 adds distributions of individual tracking errors, rather than uncertainty estimates or variability across experimental runs.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 are unchanged. New results include static32 scores of 28.72 PSNR, 0.857 SSIM and 0.092 LPIPS, with EmerNeRF higher in PSNR at 28.89; comparative runtimes; CasTrack-based Street Gaussians at 25.61 PSNR; and 2D tracking plus rigid motion at 27.69 PSNR. Figures 4–6 add editing, tracking-error and failure findings.

T1.justification: The original Gaussian, HexPlane and motion-loss formulation is retained. Section 12 expands previously described losses into explicit implementation formulas, including depth normalization, but introduces no substantive mathematical argument, new formal assumption, theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same principal claims: eliminating dependence on 3D trackers, correcting motion through guided implicit learning, and strong Waymo-NOTR/KITTI performance. Supplementary evidence and cross-references do not redefine those contributions.

C2.justification: Section 11 adds an explanation of how noisy joint pose/Gaussian optimization can degrade reconstruction across frames. Section 13 explicitly identifies inaccurate unguided human motion, other dynamic classes treated as static, and dependence on per-scene optimization. These provide substantial applicability and failure boundaries absent from v2's discussion.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies depth-loss normalization by 80 and valid depths of 0.01–80 meters, explicit loss formulas, unguided 4DGS handling of humans, and maintained object associations for editing. Existing hardware, training schedules and the promise of future public code remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography expands from 90 to 108 works, retaining the original references and adding works such as DESIRE-GS, LiDARF, GeoGaussian and ViTPose. Additions mainly extend existing citation groups and future-work discussion; the central positioning against 3D-tracker-dependent reconstruction remains stable.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain largely intact. v3 locally rewrites the ablation discussion, adds supplementary cross-references and an acknowledgment, and appends Sections 6–13. This is an appended expansion rather than extensive rewriting or reorganization.

P2.justification: v3 retains the original displays and adds Tables 4–7 and Figures 4–6, substantially expanding visual evidence through comparison tables, editing examples, error histograms and a failure case. Table 4 has minor defects: its caption mentions an absent StreetGS row, and its second-best LPIPS highlighting favors 0.142 despite the lower 0.134 entry.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens v2's existing benchmarks and ablations with a shared-trajectory motion comparison, direct tracking-error evidence, clearer loss details and explicit failure boundaries. These improve transparency and support for the retained claims. The CasTrack comparison also changes pretraining data, limiting causal interpretation, and Table 4 introduces minor presentation errors. The net gain is useful but incremental.
